messages.author: ce77ef4ebc3cf5bc
messages.subject: bifactor model identification?
parts:
Hi, experts!

I'm trying to fit a bifactor model to a reasonably large set of complete data (N = 445).  The following is the initial proposed bifactor model:

measurement.model3 <- "attitude =~ FSE11 + FSE14 + FSE15 + HO4 + HO5 + ISCO3 + ISCU4 + STR2 + STR3
                       self.efficacy =~ FSE13 + FSE16 + FSE2 + FSE6 + FSE7 + FSE8 + ISCO1 + ISMP5 + ISSH5 + FSE3 + ISCO5 + ISMP2 + ISMP3 + ISMP7 + ISSH4 + ISCO2 + ISMP6
                      structure =~ FSE11 + FSE14 + FSE15 + HO4 + HO5 + ISCO3 + ISCU4 + STR2 + STR3 + FSE13 + FSE16 + FSE2 + FSE6 + FSE7 + FSE8 + ISCO1 + ISMP5 + ISSH5 + FSE3 + ISCO5 + ISMP2 + ISMP3 + ISMP7 + ISSH4 + ISCO2 + ISMP6
                      # HO4 ~~ HO5
                      attitude ~~ self.efficacy
                      structure ~~ 0*attitude + 0*self.efficacy
                      "

That is: the general factor (called "structure" here) is theorized to affect indicators but not the specific factors.  When I submit this model to a "standard" CFA I get the following results:

 lavaan (0.5-20) converged normally after 852 iterations
  Number of observations                           445
  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic              715.942
  Degrees of freedom                               272
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000
Warning message:
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

In reading the message boards here I feel like it's implied that for a bifactor model to be identified the specific factors must be specified as uncorrelated with each other, as well as the general factor.  Is this the case?  That doesn't seem to be how bifactor models are described in the literature (e.g., Kline 2016 p320), but I am certainly no expert.  If it's not the case, what are the criteria for identifying a bifactor model?  It seems like it should be good to go.

As a followup, I am hoping to eventually add causal indicators to the structure factor, which obviously will be a problem if the model is already underidentified..

Thanks!
Jake

messages.subject: Re: bifactor model identification?
parts: In reading the message boards here I feel like it's implied that for a bifactor model to be identified the specific factors must be specified as uncorrelated with each other, as well as the general factor.  Is this the case?  That doesn't seem to be how bifactor models are described in the literature (e.g., Kline 2016 p320), but I am certainly no expert.

I think it is necessary when you have few indicators for each method/specific factor, but you might have enough indicators of each factor that you could probably freely estimate all factor covariances - but I'm not sure.  This isn't specific to lavaan, so it's probably better to post it on SEMNET.  There has been a lot of recent discussion on bifactor models, so try searching the archives first.
